population_est = }} '''Garden City Park''', historically known as '''Clowesville,''' is a [[Hamlet (New York)|hamlet]] and [[census-designated place]] (CDP) located within the [[Town of North Hempstead]] in [[Nassau County, New York|Nassau County]], on [[Long Island]], in [[New York (state)|New York]], United States. It is considered part of the Greater [[New Hyde Park, New York|New Hyde Park]] area. The population was 7,985 at the time of the 2020 census. ==History== From about 1787 until about 1874, the area was known as Clowesville, which was then the [[County seat|County Seat]] of [[Queens|Queens County]], and contained the county courthouse and jail.{{Cite book|last=Winsche|first=Richard|title=The History of Nassau County Community Place-Names|date=October 1, 1999|publisher=Empire State Books|isbn=978-1557871541|location=[[Interlaken, New York]]}} The community's name was eventually changed to Garden City Park due to its proximity to the then-new development of [[Garden City, New York|Garden City]]. On December 7, 1993, six people were killed and nineteen were injured in [[1993 Long Island Rail Road shooting|a racially-motivated mass shooting]] aboard an eastbound [[Long Island Rail Road]] train at the [[Merillon Avenue station|Merillion Avenue station]] – Garden City Park's local LIRR station.{{Cite news |last=Barron |first=James |date=1993-12-09 |title=DEATH ON THE L.I.R.R.: The Overview; Portrait of Suspect Emerges in Shooting on L.I. Train |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1993/12/09/nyregion/death-lirr-overview-portrait-suspect-emerges-shooting-li-train.html |access-date=2022-08-03 |issn=0362-4331}} ==Geography== [[File:GardenCityPark.NY.CDP2000.gif|thumb|left|U.S. Census map of Garden City Park]] According to the [[United States Census Bureau]], the CDP has a total area of {{convert|1|sqmi|km2}}, all land.{{cite web|date=2011-02-12|title=US Gazetteer files: 2010, 2000, and 1990|url=https://www.census.gov/geographies/reference-files/time-series/geo/gazetteer-files.html|access-date=2011-04-23|publisher=[[United States Census Bureau]]}} Garden City Park is bordered by [[New York State Route 25B|Hillside Avenue]] to the north, [[County Route 8 (Nassau County, New York)|Herricks Road]] to the east, and Denton Avenue to the west.{{Cite web |title=Long Island Zoning Atlas |url=https://www.longislandzoningatlas.org/map?layers=villages_inc%2Cvillages_uninc%2Clirr%2Ctown%2Creservations |access-date=2021-09-07 |website=www.longislandzoningatlas.org}} The southern border is the boundary of the Town of North Hempstead with the [[Town of Hempstead]], roughly coinciding with Atlantic Avenue and the [[Main Line (Long Island Rail Road)|Main Line]] of the [[Long Island Rail Road|Long Island Rail Road (LIRR)]]. The local LIRR station – partially located within Garden City Park and partially in the Village of Garden City – is [[Merillon Avenue (LIRR station)|Merillon Avenue]]. Some local and town maps reflect that Garden City Park spills over north into Herricks. Mail delivery is provided by the New Hyde Park Post Office utilizing the 11040 ZIP Code. A suburb of [[New York City]], the hamlet is located approximately {{convert|20|mi}} to the east of [[Midtown Manhattan]]. ===Climate===
According to the [[Köppen climate classification]], Garden City Park has a [[Humid subtropical climate]] (type Cfa) with cool, wet winters and hot, humid summers.{{Cite web |title=Interactive United ==Demographics== {{US Census population |2000= 7554 |2010= 7806 |2020= 7985 |footnote=U.S. Decennial Census{{cite web|url=http://www.census.gov/prod/www/decennial.html|title=Census of Population and Housing|publisher=Census.gov|accessdate=June 4, 2016}} |align = right |align-fn = center }} ===2020 census=== As of the [[2020 United States census|2020 census]], Garden City Park had a population of 7,985. The median age was 44.1 years. 19.9% of residents were under the age of 18 and 21.7% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 96.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 94.8 males age 18 and over.{{cite web|title=2020 Decennial Census Demographic Profile (DP1)|url=https://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/dp?get=NAME,DP1_0021P,DP1_0024P,DP1_0025C,DP1_0049C,DP1_0045C,DP1_0069C,DP1_0073C,DP1_0125P,DP1_0126P,DP1_0129P,DP1_0133P,DP1_0137P,DP1_0138P,DP1_0139P,DP1_0141P,DP1_0142P,DP1_0143P,DP1_0145P,DP1_0146P,DP1_0147C,DP1_0148C,DP1_0149C,DP1_0156C,DP1_0157C,DP1_0158C,DP1_0159P,DP1_0160P&for=place%3A28189&in=state%3A36|website=United States Census Bureau|year=2021|access-date=April 30, 2026|df=mdy}}{{cite web|title=2020 Decennial Census Redistricting Data (Public Law 94-171)|url=https://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/pl?get=NAME,P1_001N,P1_003N,P1_004N,P1_005N,P1_006N,P1_007N,P1_008N,P1_009N,P2_001N,P2_002N,H1_001N,H1_002N&for=place%3A28189&in=state%3A36|website=United States Census Bureau|year=2021|access-date=April 30, 2026|df=mdy}} 100.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.0% lived in rural areas.{{cite web|title=2020 Decennial Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics (DHC)|url=https://api.census.gov/data/2020/dec/dhc?get=NAME,P2_002N,P2_003N&for=place%3A28189&in=state%3A36|website=United States Census Bureau|year=2023|access-date=April 30, 2026|df=mdy}} There were 2,499 households in Garden City Park, of which 35.8% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 66.1% were married-couple households, 11.7% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 19.8% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 15.6% of all households were made up of individuals and 10.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. There were 2,592 housing units, of which 3.6% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.9% and the rental vacancy rate was 2.6%. {| class="wikitable" |+ Racial composition as of the 2020 census ! Race !! Number !! Percent |- | [[White Americans|White]] || 2,839 || 35.6% |- | [[African Americans|Black or African American]] || 231 || 2.9% |- | [[Native Americans in the United States|American Indian and Alaska Native]] || 37 || 0.5% |- | [[Asian Americans|Asian]] || 3,747 || 46.9% |- | [[Native Hawaiians|Native Hawaiian]] and [[Pacific Islander|Other Pacific Islander]] || 2 || 0.0% |- | Some other race || 500 || 6.3% |- | [[Multiracial Americans|Two or more races]] || 629 || 7.9% |- | ''[[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic or Latino]] (of any race)'' || 999 || 12.5% |} ===2010 census=== As of the [[census]]{{cite web |url=https://www.census.gov |publisher=[[United States Census Bureau]] |access-date=2008-01-31 |title=U.S. Census website }} of 2010, there were 7,806 people, 2,508 households, and 1,993 families living in the CDP. The population density was {{convert|7,759.3|PD/sqmi|PD/km2|sp=us|adj=off}}. There were 2,548 housing units at an average density of {{convert|2,617.3|/sqmi|/km2|sp=us|adj=off}}. The racial makeup of the CDP was 48.6% [[Non-Hispanic Whites|Non-Hispanic White]], 3.8% [[African American (U.S. Census)|African American]], 0.3% [[Native American (U.S. Census)|Native American]], 33.1% [[Asian (U.S. Census)|Asian]], 0.1% [[Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)|Pacific Islander]], 3.8% from [[Race (United States Census)|other races]], and 2.6% from two or more races. [[Hispanic (U.S. Census)|Hispanic]] or [[Latino (U.S. Census)|Latino]] of any race were 12.1% of the population. There were 2,508 households, out of which 33.9% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 66.3% were married couples living together, 9.9% had a female householder with no husband present, and 20.5% were non-families. 18.2% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 3.01 and the average family size was 3.43. In the CDP, the population was spread out, with 22.4% under the age of 18, 7.5% from 18 to 24, 26.3% from 25 to 44, 24.8% from 45 to 64, and 19.0% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 41 years. For every 100 females, there were 92.5 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 88.1 males. The median income for a household in the CDP was $74,746, and the median income for a family was $81,580. Males had a median income of $47,234 versus $38,580 for females. The [[per capita income]] for the CDP was $29,250. About 0.4% of families and 1.0% of the population were below the [[poverty line]], including 0.3% of those under age 18 and 2.2% of those age 65 or over. ===2000 census=== As of the [[census]] of 2000, there were 7,554 people, 2,508 households, and 1,993 families living in the CDP. The population density was {{convert|7,759.3|PD/sqmi|PD/km2|sp=us|adj=off}}. There were 2,548 housing units at an average density of {{convert|2,617.3|/sqmi|/km2|sp=us|adj=off}}. The racial makeup of the CDP was 70.20% White, 4.21% African American, 0.28% Native American, 20.49% Asian, 0.03% Pacific Islander, 2.13% from other races, and 2.66% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 8.09% of the population. There were 2,508 households, out of which 33.9% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 66.3% were [[Marriage|married couples]] living together, 9.9% had a female householder with no husband present, and 20.5% were non-families. 18.2% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 3.01 and the average family size was 3.43. In the CDP, the population was spread out, with 22.4% under the age of 18, 7.5% from 18 to 24, 26.3% from 25 to 44, 24.8% from 45 to 64, and 19.0% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 41 years. For every 100 females, there were 92.5 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 88.1 males. The median income for a household in the CDP was $74,746, and the median income for a family was $81,580. Males had a median income of $47,234 versus $38,580 for females. The [[per capita income]] for the CDP was $29,250. About 0.4% of families and 1.0% of the population were below the [[poverty line]], including 0.3% of those under age 18 and 2.2% of those age 65 or over. ==Government== ===Town representation=== As an unincorporated area of the Town of North Hempstead, Garden City Park is directly governed by said Town, which is seated in [[Manhasset, New York|Manhasset]]. Garden City Park is split between the Town of North Hempstead's and 3rd and 4th council districts, which as of August 2025 are represented on the [[North Hempstead Town Council]] by Dennis J. Walsh ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]–[[Mineola, New York|Mineola]]) and Christine Liu ([[Democratic Party (United States)|D]]–[[Herricks, New York|Herricks]]), respectively.{{Cite web |title=District 3 - Dennis Walsh |url=https://www.northhempsteadny.gov/government/councilmembers/district_3.php |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=www.northhempsteadny.gov |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=District 4 - Christine Liu |url=https://www.northhempsteadny.gov/government/councilmembers/district_4.php |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=www.northhempsteadny.gov |language=en}} ====County representation==== Garden City Park is located within Nassau County's 9th Legislative district, which as of August 2025 is represented in the [[Nassau County Legislature]] by Scott Strauss (R–Mineola).{{Cite web |title=District 9 - Scott Strauss |url=https://www.nassaucountyny.gov/523/District-9---Scott-Strauss |access-date=2025-08-20 |website=www.nassaucountyny.gov}} ====State representation==== =====New York State Assembly===== Garden City Park is split between the [[New York State Assembly]]'s [[New York's 16th State Assembly district|16th]] and [[New York's 19th State Assembly district|19th State Assembly districts]], which as of August 2025 are represented in the New York State Assembly by [[Daniel Norber|Daniel J. Norber]] (R–[[Great Neck, New York|Great Neck]]) and [[Ed Ra|Edward P. Ra]] (R–[[Garden City South, New York|Garden City South]]), respectively.{{Cite web |title=Daniel J. Norber – Assembly District 16 {{!}}Assembly Member Directory {{!}} New York State Assembly |url=https://nyassembly.gov/mem/Daniel-J-Norber/bio/ |access-date=January 1, 2025 |website=nyassembly.gov}}{{cite web |last=Walker |first=Corey |date=November 11, 2024 |title=Ex-IDF Soldier Becomes First Republican in 50 Years to Win New York State Assembly Seat in Long Island District |url=https://www.algemeiner.com/2024/11/11/ex-idf-soldier-becomes-first-republican-50-years-win-new-york-state-assembly-seat-long-island-district/ |accessdate=November 15, 2024 |website=The Algemeiner}}{{Cite web |title=Edward P. Ra - Assembly District 19 {{!}}Assembly Member Directory {{!}} New York State Assembly |url=https://nyassembly.gov/mem/Edward-P-Ra/office/ |access-date=2024-08-13 |website=nyassembly.gov}} =====New York State Senate===== Garden City Park is located in the [[New York State Senate]]'s [[New York's 7th State Senate district|7th State Senate district]], which as of August 2025 is represented in the New York State Senate by [[Jack Martins|Jack M. Martins]] (R–[[Old Westbury, New York|Old Westbury]]).{{Cite web |title=NY Senate District 7 |url=https://www.nysenate.gov/district/7 |access-date=2020-12-18 |website=NY State Senate}} ====Federal representation==== =====United States Congress===== Garden City Park is located within [[New York's 3rd congressional district|New York's 3rd Congressional district]], which as of August 2025 is represented in the [[United States Congress]] by [[Tom Suozzi|Thomas R. Suozzi]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|D]]–[[Glen Cove, New York|Glen Cove]]).{{Cite news |last=Fandos |first=Nicholas |date=February 29, 2024 |title=Tom Suozzi Returns to Congress With 2 Words for House: 'Wake Up' |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/02/28/nyregion/tom-suozzi-speech-congress.html |access-date=March 1, 2024 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} =====United States Senate===== Like the rest of New York, Garden City Park is represented in the [[United States Senate]] by [[Chuck Schumer|Charles Schumer]] (D) and [[Kirsten Gillibrand]] (D).{{Cite web |title=U.S. Senate: Contacting U.S. Senators |url=https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm?State=NY |access-date=2021-07-22 |website=www.senate.gov}} ===Politics=== In the [[2024 United States presidential election]], roughly half of Garden City Park voters voted for [[Donald Trump|Donald J. Trump]] (R), while the other half voted for [[Kamala D. Harris]] (D).{{Cite web |last=LaRocco |first=Paul |date=2024-11-13 |title=Map: How Long Island voted for president in Harris-Trump race |url=https://www.newsday.com/long-island/politics/elections/trump-harris-election-results-uuvmm1tu |access-date=2024-11-19 |website=Newsday |language=en}} ==Education== Garden City Park is divided among these school districts:{{cite web|url=https://www2.census.gov/geo/maps/DC2020/PL20/st36_ny/schooldistrict_maps/c36059_nassau/DC20SD_C36059.pdf|title=2020 CENSUS - SCHOOL DISTRICT REFERENCE MAP: Nassau County, NY|publisher=[[U.S. Census Bureau]]|access-date=2023-11-10}} * [[New Hyde Park-Garden City Park Union Free School District]] and [[Sewanhaka Central High School District]] * [[Herricks Union Free School District]] * [[Mineola Union Free School District]] Additionally, [[Mineola High School (New York)|Mineola High School]] is located within the hamlet. ==See also== * [[Garden City South, New York]] * [[East Garden City, New York]] ==References== {{Commons category|Garden City Park, New York}} {{NorthHempsteadNY}} {{Nassau County, New York}} {{authority control}} [[Category:Town of North Hempstead, New York]] [[Category:Census-designated places in New York (state)]] [[Category:Census-designated places in Nassau County, New York]] [[Category:Former county seats in New York (state)]]
